consensus_findings.description: D6 says dispatcher/orchestrator profiles 'explicitly receive' `report_vendor_rate_limit`, but no artifact names the mechanism or owner. `authorize_operation` -> `policy_engine.check_operation` routes any operation outside READ/WRITE/ADMIN_ACTIONS to the profile's `allowed_operations`; that list is derived solely by `derive_allowed_operations` from `CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS`/`TRUST_DERIVED_OPERATIONS`/`UNIVERSAL_OPERATIONS` in `agents_config.py`, is a `SYNC_TRACKED_FIELD` overwritten by profile sync at boot, and an unmapped capability in agents.yaml raises ValueError. Task 1.4 declares only location/policy_vendor/catalog_vendor; no task in 1.x/2.x adds the operation to the derivation. wp-api-watchdog (task 3.1 tests 'report operation, 403') cannot write `agents_config.py` or `agents.yaml` (only wp-registry-core may), so the package that must prove the grant cannot create it and the package that can create it is not told to.

Two wp-integration gates are not executable as written. (a) mypy discovers config only from cwd; there is no repo-root pyproject.toml, so running from `cwd: '.'` drops `[tool.mypy] ignore_missing_imports = true` from `agent-coordinator/pyproject.toml` and diverges from CI (`uv run mypy src/` with working-directory agent-coordinator). (b) 'Coordinator regression' runs `pytest agent-coordinator/tests -q` with no marker filter, so `e2e` tests needing running services are included, whereas CI runs `-m "not e2e and not integration"`. Either the gate fails on the merged tree for reasons unrelated to dg-01, or it imposes a services-up precondition no package declares.

Critical: D6/spec require dispatcher/orchestrator principals to hold `report_vendor_rate_limit` so trust-2 orchestrators can report a dispatched lane that differs from their own. Projected allowlists are derived only from `UNIVERSAL_OPERATIONS` / `CAPABILITY_OPERATIONS` / `TRUST_DERIVED_OPERATIONS` in `agents_config.py`, and unknown operations fall through to that allowlist in `policy_engine.py`. No task names adding the grant, `wp-api-watchdog` cannot write the grant seam, and `change-context` attributes auth only to `coordination_api.py`/`vendor_registry.py`. Without the grant, cross-lane observation POSTs remain 403 for the real collector topology.

Postgres-backed gates pass vacuously. `tests/integration/postgres/conftest.py` calls `pytest.skip("PostgreSQL not running")` when the DSN is unreachable, so `test_fresh_database_migration.py` (wp-registry-core and wp-integration) and the concurrent RPC tests for bounded reset, replay conflict, and compaction (task 2.3) exit 0 with zero tests executed. `expect_exit_code: 0` cannot distinguish 'atomic RPC replay/compaction verified' from 'skipped'. D1 rejects this pattern for the deployment test but the package gates do not apply the same rule.

Model-scoped limits (D4, spec 'Model-scoped limit has an alternate model', SQL `scope='model'`) have no producer. In `review_dispatcher.py` capacity errors are consumed inside the adapter's model-fallback loop (`models_attempted` grows; `error_class=CAPACITY` is set only when every model fails). `ReviewResult` carries `vendor`, `model_used`, `models_attempted` but no `agent_id`, and D7/task 4.4 mandate 'once per result'. A run where model A returns 429 and fallback B succeeds yields a successful result with no capacity class, so the collector reports nothing and the A limit is never persisted. Nothing in tasks 4.3/4.4 states that intermediate per-model capacity failures become `scope=model` observations.

The event schema and SQL contract contradict each other for `kind=probe`, and task 1.1 requires semantic parity between them. The schema requires `observation_id` and `source_agent_id` for every observation, but `vendor_probe_state` has no `observation_id` column (PK is `agent_id`) and names the producer `source`, not `source_agent_id`. D3/D4 never define a probe observation id. A parity test cannot pass against both artifacts as written.

D6 and D9 rely on bridge clients distinguishing `unknown_vendor_lane` from `vendor_registry_unavailable`, but the contract does not bind that promise: the 404/409 responses carry only `description` text and no `content` schema referencing `Problem`, so parity tests cannot assert the body; `vendor_registry_unavailable` appears in the enum but no path or status code emits it (no 503 anywhere); and the coordinator's existing problem+json handlers emit RFC 7807 `type/title/status/detail` with the reason in a `urn:` `type`, not a `code` field. The bridge today maps every 404 to `route_unavailable`, so without a bound body schema the older-coordinator vs bad-lane distinction has no deterministic wire form.

`dispatch_agent_id` has readers but no writer. The orchestrator reads it from `context` to choose exact-lane vs legacy provider-scope handling, D8 says policy returns `to_agent_id`, and D7 says `provider_dispatch.py` gains an optional `agent_id` never inferred from provider. No artifact states who places the selected lane into the orchestrator `context` for the next dispatch or into `PhaseDispatchPayload.agent_id` (today the payload is only constructed by tests and the smoke script; the orchestrator's `dispatch_fn` is injected by the prompt layer). Without a named writer every roadmap limit takes the ambiguous legacy path and the exact-attribution scenarios in wp-roadmap-policy are dead code in production.

Nit: D2/spec say configured base URL constrains the catalog join, but dg-00 `model_catalog` uniqueness and `CatalogService.get_entry` key only `(vendor, model, endpoint_kind)`, and OpenAPI `CatalogModelPrice` exposes no `base_url`. Implementers cannot use base URL as a join key without inventing a filter rule outside the contract.

Nit: D1/spec require a deployment test that persists at least one probe snapshot under `SKILLS_ROOT` + `AGENTS_YAML`, but `wp-api-watchdog` verification only runs unit pytest suites and existing Dockerfile/import packaging tests are outside its `write_allow`. The packaging requirement therefore has no executable package gate.

Nit: D5 and tasks 2.3/2.6 require SQL RPCs for atomic probe upsert, rate-limit insert/replay/conflict, and compaction, and D11 says contracts land before registry/RPC core, but `contracts/db/schema.sql` defines only tables/index. `wp-contracts` has no task to publish function signatures/return codes, so concurrent RPC TDD cannot lock the boundary before migration work.
none: Revision 3 assigns every runtime seam and integration dependency, preserves typed lane/provider/policy/catalog identities and explicit location, and keeps model pricing solely in dg-00.
none: Probe and limit evidence now have deterministic freshness, bounded reset, atomic replay, compaction ownership, explicit unavailable behavior, and validation gates.

D5 requires a future `reset_at` but allows `retry_after_seconds: 0`, which normalizes to `reset_at == receipt time`; under D4's `now >= reset_at` is expired rule the observation is accepted (202, stored, audited) and immediately inert. The two reset inputs have different validity rules for the same instant.

`dispatchable` is a required `VendorLane` field and the spec lists 'dispatchability', but neither design nor spec defines it or its relation to `availability.available` (adapter configured? transport reachable? available and not limited?). Two implementers can produce different, both-'correct' values, and D8 does not say whether the roadmap filter chain uses it.

Latent join gap for local lanes: dg-00's `LocalEndpointService.sync_from_agents_config` registers an `endpoint_kind=local` lane in `model_catalog` with `vendor=agent.type` and `model=agent.sdk.model or agent.name`. A local lane without `sdk.model` is catalogued under its lane name, which is not in the 'authored CLI/SDK ∪ provider map' set, so the D4 step-2 local gate would always report it unknown/unavailable. No bundled lane currently sets `endpoint_kind: local`, so this is unreachable today, but dg-04 will add them.

Optional: D4/spec define model-scoped limits that keep a lane available when another model remains, while D7/tasks require reporting capacity once per result after the dispatcher finishes. Current `review_dispatcher` exhausts model fallbacks then returns one terminal capacity failure, which naturally becomes lane-scoped. No task assigns mid-chain `scope=model` producers, so the alternate-model scenario is only exercisable via direct API POSTs unless that producer is named.

FYI: `work-packages.yaml` declares `plan_revision: 3`, but `change-context.md` remediation still says plan revision 2 incorporated the first panel. Traceability readers can mis-identify the current normative revision.

Revision 3 closes the previously blocking seams for typed lane/provider/policy/catalog identity with explicit location, endpoint-kind-local catalog gating, lane-vs-model limit precedence, legacy provider-scoped exclusion, request-quote/cost_guard behavior, bridge→policy package ordering, compaction ownership, and tier-A executable gates including mypy/DAG/migration/contract re-runs.

Probe freshness, first-poll persistence without transitions, no_probe_method snapshots, bounded reset/replay hashing, fail-closed registry defaults, and watchdog-scheduled compaction now have coherent owners across D4–D5/D10 and tasks 2.x/3.x.
